body:
Fabro Anywhere — your computer's AI on your phone

- Phone app (installable PWA at /app/ on the website, EN/FR/ES/DE, light/dark): pairs by reading the computer's circular code with the camera (or typing it), conversations offline in IndexedDB, messages queued while the computer is away, two-way sync with conflict-free merging, streaming answers, photos to vision models, agent permission prompts, dictation and hands-free voice mode (computer's Whisper/Piper, else the phone's own speech), notifications, and a small model on the phone (WebLLM, WebGPU)
- Circular pairing code: data rings of arcs around the propeller, Reed-Solomon protected, revealed by a circular sweep; read from camera frames in a worker (rotation, tilt, blur, both themes)
- Security: P-256 keys exchanged at pairing (proofs over the code's secret), AES-GCM end to end; public MQTT relays only put devices in touch (or carry ciphertext as a fallback); direct WebRTC channel when possible; your own relay supported (scripts/mqtt-relay.js)
- Computer: Settings › Fabro Anywhere (pair, rename, remove phones, relays, TURN), hidden network window, phone runs use the desktop's prompt/tools/model, Web Push sent straight to the phone's push service (RFC 8291/8292), agent-task notifications, removed phones are told so
- Tests: core, code reading, and a full computer ↔ phone run (fake camera, local relay) in CI
- Website: Anywhere page with the phone app, privacy section for Anywhere

Fabro website

- Website in site/: home "Lift off, locally." with the animated propeller and app screenshots, feature pages (Chat, Agent, Code, Voice, Anywhere), "Can my PC run it?" (graphics card + RAM → recommended models, same catalog and fit rules as the installer), privacy, changelog from GitHub Releases, legal notice with third-party licences
- Smart download: detects Windows / macOS / Linux and links the right file of the latest release (Fabro-Installer.exe, .dmg, .AppImage), with the other platforms one click away
- English by default, French / Spanish / German from the browser language or the switcher; light / dark theme with the app's colours; works without JavaScript; no cookies or trackers
- Static build (node site/build.js), netlify.toml, built in CI; release notes are now written from the release commit message
- Images: when a Metal / Vulkan driver fails on large buffers, retry with the text encoder and VAE on the processor

Accessibility, separate tool runtime, opt-in crash reports

- Accessibility: every clickable element reachable and usable with the keyboard, icon buttons named, menus with arrow keys / Home / End / Escape (focus returns to the opener), dialogs trap focus, skip link to the message box, visible focus rings, screen-reader announcements (answer done, errors, permission requests), in-app 'Reduce animations' (also follows the system), forced colours; e2e runs axe-core (WCAG 2 A/AA): no violations
- Tool runtime: commands from tools (terminal, Python, tests, lint, git, Code terminal) run in a separate Electron utility process, restarted automatically; permissions stay in the main process
- Crash reports: nothing collected or sent by default; opt-in keeps reports locally and offers a pre-filled GitHub issue the user reviews and sends (home paths masked)

Installer picks the engine and the first model; clean uninstall

- Installer detects the hardware (GPU + real VRAM from the driver / nvidia-smi, RAM, disks) and shows the engine it will use (CUDA / Vulkan / processor)
- New step 'Your first AI model': the 3 best models for this PC (same catalogue and fit rules as the app) or 'choose later', and the disk to store models on (free space checked)
- The choice is seeded in settings: Fabro starts the download on first launch, into that disk (a new model library when it isn't the system disk)
- Uninstaller asks whether to also delete conversations, settings, memories and downloaded models (never during updates or silent uninstalls); the app keeps the list of its model folders for it

Local image creation with stable-diffusion.cpp

- stable-diffusion.cpp release build picked per computer (CUDA 12 + cudart / Vulkan / Metal / CPU)
- Two models: SD Turbo (2 GB, 512 px, works on CPU) and Z-Image Turbo (6.7 GB, 1024 px, GPU 6 GB+), recommended from the hardware; installed from Settings or on first use (dependency card)
- generate_image tool in chat: aspect ratios, seed, negative prompt; live progress, shimmer placeholder, image card (open, show in folder, zoom); saved in Documents/Fabro/Images
- Release lookup falls back to the GitHub release page when the API is rate-limited
- CI: real image generated on Linux, Windows and macOS

Local voice — dictation and voice mode with scene

- Voice stack installed on demand in its own venv: Whisper (faster-whisper, CTranslate2 int8) for speech to text, Piper for speech; curated FR/EN/ES/DE voices; models from Hugging Face
- Dictation: mic button in the composer, ends on silence
- Voice mode: live conversation with voice activity detection, interruption (speak or Space), subtitles, voice picker, mute; answers spoken sentence by sentence while they stream
- Scene: show_on_scene tool shows web images / videos (SearXNG), pages, or SVG/HTML the AI draws
- Fabro propeller spins slowly when listening, faster when thinking, fastest and pulsing when speaking
- Microphone permission for the app page only; CSP allows https images/frames for the scene
- CI: voice smoke test on Linux and Windows (real install, fake microphone, spoken question)
- Tests updated for the tools section of chat prompts; agent-real regex fixed

Agents that actually act, with any model

- Dynamic agent system prompt built per turn: the exact tools sent (name, args, purpose), a strict work loop, a worked example, truthfulness rules (never 'I can't access', never invent results), error recovery, safety; chat mode gets a tools section too; sub-agents and Code mode included
- Runtime guards: a model that refuses, claims undone work, announces a step and stops, answers an action request with text only, returns nothing, or leaves its plan unfinished is sent back to work
- Tool calls written as text are executed: <tool_call>, <function=…>, [TOOL_CALLS], <|python_tag|>, fenced JSON, bare JSON — known tools only, text retracted from the answer
- Precise errors: unknown tool (lists the real ones), invalid JSON (shows the schema), empty write, no-op edit, repeated failing call, repeated identical call
- Context budget: old tool results shortened, oldest steps dropped before the window overflows; local engine crash mid-task → reload and retry once
- Leaked </think> moved to reasoning; folder-name case fixed on Linux; read_file numbers lines only on long files; edit_file strips copied line numbers; run_command defaults to Documents/Fabro
- CI: real Qwen3.5 4B agent test on Fabro's engine

Projects with instructions, shared files and local semantic search

- Projects page: create, describe, instructions, files (drop or pick), project chats
- Files indexed locally: PDF (pdf.js), DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/ODT, HTML, text and code; chunked
- Hybrid search: SQLite FTS5 keywords + EmbeddingGemma vectors (fusion), optional Qwen3 reranker
- Small projects are given whole to the model; large ones get the best passages + project_search tool
- Engine: embedding / reranking servers; embedding models kept out of the chat model list
- Engine smoke test checks semantic search on Windows, macOS and Linux

Code mode V1

- Open a project folder: explorer with git badges, recent projects, code sessions per project
- Agent always on in code sessions, scoped to the project (relative paths, commands run there)
- Permissions per project: ask before acting / accept edits / auto, 'always for this project'
- Sandbox: commands outside the project folder or touching outside paths ask first
- Modified-file cards (+/-), Diff / File / Preview viewer, editor with highlighting and line numbers
- Terminal panel: Terminal, Tests (summary + failures) and Problems tabs; run_tests / run_lint tools
- Git: branches, commit, discard, history, undo last commit; MinGit installed on demand on Windows
- Undo an agent turn (checkpoints), project instructions (FABRO.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md)
- Qwen3 Coder / Qwen2.5 Coder recommended in Code mode
- SearXNG runs on Windows (pwd shim)

Sub-agents, session panel, SearXNG search, AI browser with tabs

- Sub-agents: run_subagent delegates self-contained work to nested agent runs (parallel when called together, steps nested in the UI, permissions asked in place)
- update_plan tool + session panel (Progression / Sorties / Utilisés dans cette session)
- SearXNG: private instance installed on demand (Python venv), or your own instance; DuckDuckGo fallback; categories, time range, answers and infobox
- Agent browser: tabs, browser_search, browser_extract (readable Markdown), find, select, wait; ad/tracker blocking and cookie banners refused automatically
- Code-mode backend (project tree, git, terminal, tests/lint parsing)
- Fix: skipped view transitions no longer throw when the window is hidden

Agent V1 — automatic agent mode, files, terminal, built-in browser, documents, Python, MCP, skills, permissions

- Calling any tool other than web search / fetch switches the conversation to agent mode: badge, agent system prompt, the in-flight call continues; workspace panel with steps, live browser and changed files
- Tools: list/read/write/edit/delete/search files in allowed folders; run_command (PowerShell/bash, live output, secrets stripped from env); create_document (DOCX, PDF, slides PDF, XLSX, CSV, MD, HTML, also saved as artifacts); run_python with a private Python installed on demand ('Installer les dépendances' card); load_skill (Claude-compatible SKILL.md folders, ~/.claude/skills found automatically)
- Built-in browser: isolated WebContentsView (own session), visible live, take/give back control; open, read (interactive elements with ids), click, type, keys, scroll, zoom, screenshot (sent to vision models), back, script
- MCP client: stdio + Streamable HTTP with OAuth (dynamic registration, PKCE), import from Claude Desktop config; tools selected by relevance with a token gauge
- Permissions per tool (always / ask / never) and per folder; guardrails: purchases, sending, publishing, deleting, downloads and risky commands always confirm; passwords and card fields are never typed; credential folders are never readable; tool output wrapped as untrusted data
- Models without native tool calling fall back to <tool_call> JSON parsing
- Tests: agent runtime test + e2e covering permissions, files, docx, browser password guard and an MCP server

Chat V1 — web search & fetch tools, branches, thinking control, styles, memory, ephemeral chats, editable artifacts, SQLite

Chat
- Tool loop for OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic APIs; chat tools: web search (DuckDuckGo, Brave, Ducky) and fetch_url; steps and cited sources shown in the answer; models without tool support fall back automatically
- Thinking control in the composer (auto / off / low / medium / high) for llama.cpp, OpenAI-style and Claude
- Edit any message → new branch; regenerate keeps the old answer; ‹ 2/3 › navigation between versions
- Response styles (concise, explanatory, formal) and custom styles learned from a writing sample
- Memory: durable facts extracted in the background, editable and deletable, injected into the prompt
- Ephemeral chats (never saved, no memory); AI conversation titles; system notification when an answer finishes in the background
- Artifacts: documents, slides, web pages, SVG and code as cards; side panel with preview/source, rich editing of text and colors, slide themes and presenter mode, versions with restore; export to DOCX, PDF, HTML, MD, SVG; HTML runs in a sandboxed fabro-art:// iframe; gallery page
- Personalization page: name, custom instructions, styles, memory
Architecture
- SQLite (node:sqlite) for conversations with FTS5 full-text search in the sidebar, memories and artifacts; JSON conversations imported on first run
Fixes: composer text could reappear after very fast answers; settings re-renders no longer wipe forms being typed;
boot waits for every renderer script.

Engine V1 — multi-model pool, per-model profiles, memory planner, storage, local API

Engine
- Several models loaded at once; least-recently-used idle model unloaded when memory is full
- Per-model profiles: context, GPU layers, threads, KV cache (F16/Q8/Q4), flash attention, MoE experts in RAM, preload (on demand / at startup / always), idle unload, generation overrides
- Memory planner from GGUF metadata: VRAM/RAM estimate before loading and automatic GPU/RAM split
- Prompt cache reuse, flash attention auto, --cpu-moe for MoE models that don't fit the GPU
- Power modes (auto battery saver), process priority; automatic + one-click rollback to the previous engine build
- Resource monitor (VRAM, GPU load/temp, RAM, CPU, per-model memory), readable logs, token usage history
- Local OpenAI-compatible API (models from the engine and providers), optional key and LAN access
- Discreet notification when only the engine updates
Models & storage
- Model libraries on any disk, move models between disks, import from Ollama / LM Studio / folders without copying
- Download queue with pause/resume, parallel limit, speed limit, free-space check; SHA-256 verification after download and on demand
Tests: engine smoke covers import + KV profile + two models + local API; e2e covers the new tabs.

External providers, tray, AI hotkey + quick bar

- Providers layer separate from the built-in llama.cpp engine: OpenAI, Anthropic (native Messages API), xAI Grok, Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, Together, Cerebras, Perplexity, any OpenAI-compatible server; Ollama and LM Studio detected and connected in one click
- API keys encrypted with the OS keychain (safeStorage) in secrets.json, never sent to the renderer
- Legacy Ollama settings migrated; selectedModel no longer deep-merged
- Close button hides to tray; tray menu; start at login (hidden); system notifications
- Global AI shortcut (Ctrl+Win+Space, Copilot key) opens a quick bar that continues the current conversation or starts a new one (Tab), streams the answer, opens in Fabro
- Installer: optional 'external providers' on first install
- Tests: offline provider adapter tests + Electron/Playwright end-to-end UI test in CI

Standalone Fabro-Installer.exe (Rust + WebView2) with its own UI

- Fetches latest.yml, downloads with live progress, verifies SHA-512, silent NSIS install, launches Fabro
- Update mode when Fabro is already installed; classic NSIS fallback without WebView2
- CI builds the installer and attaches it to the release

Engine download works without the GitHub API

- Keep pre-releases (llama.cpp may flag them), only skip drafts
- If the API fails or lists nothing usable, read tags from the public releases Atom feed and probe the predictable download URLs (CUDA 12.4 / 13.x, Vulkan, CPU)
- Error message now says why each source failed

Fix 'No compatible engine build'

llama.cpp publishes a release before its binaries are uploaded, so /releases/latest
can have no assets. Walk the 10 most recent releases and take the first one that
carries a build for this machine. Prefer CUDA 12 over 13 (older drivers), clearer
error with platform/arch/accel, explicit GitHub rate-limit message.

Motion system + faster, more visible propeller loader

- Propeller loader: faster spin, readable blades with motion-blur trail and glow, larger
- Hero propeller spins in on the welcome screen
- View transitions between views, slide on back/forward, circular reveal on theme switch
- Message entrance, streaming caret, send-button launch, press/hover feedback
- Boot stagger, settings tab transitions, shimmering progress bars, engine-ready pop
Fabro v0.1.0 — base app (UI + chat), local engine, models, dev mode, release workflow
